key_insight: OpenSearch-VL provides a fully open, end-to-end recipe (data, trajectory synthesis, and training procedures) to build reproducible frontier multimodal search agents that perform deep search, evidence verification, and multi-step reasoning across images and text.
problem_solved: Addresses the reproducibility gap caused by missing open high-quality training data, opaque trajectory synthesis pipelines, and absent training recipes for top-tier multimodal search agents.
method: Curate and release open multimodal training data and search trajectories tailored for deep search tasks (active retrieval, evidence checking, multi-step reasoning).
Design a transparent trajectory synthesis pipeline that simulates agent search behaviors and verification steps to produce training signals.
Train a retrieval-augmented multimodal model using the synthesized trajectories and verification supervision to teach multi-step, evidence-based reasoning over images and text.
impact: Makes state-of-the-art multimodal search agent development reproducible and accessible, accelerating research, benchmarking, and practical deployment by lowering the barrier to replicate and extend frontier agent capabilities.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: data sources → trajectory synthesis → retrieval/verification → model training → agent behavior
Before vs. after diagram: opaque closed-source stack vs. open recipe with modular components
Example multimodal query trace: image + query → retrieved evidence snippets → reasoning steps → final answer (annotated)
Bar chart or checklist illustrating reproducibility benefits (open data, open code, transparent pipeline, repeatable training)
paper_title: OpenSearch-VL: An Open Recipe for Frontier Multimodal Search Agents
paper_authors: Shuang Chen, Kaituo Feng, Hangting Chen, Wenxuan Huang, Dasen Dai
